title: Latvia Faces Coalition Uncertainty and Fiscal Squeeze · 24 Oct
keywords: Latvia, coalition government, Andris Kulbergs, United List, National Alliance, New Unity, Latvian election, austerity, fiscal deficit, public debt, European Commission, GDP, minimum wage, public sector, EU fiscal rules, Baltic states
notes: Latvia's October election produced no outright winner, leaving Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs locked in protracted coalition negotiations while the country confronts a widening budget deficit and promises of austerity without tax rises. A three-party bloc of United List, the National Alliance, and New Unity could secure a workable parliamentary majority, but the policy compromises required to hold it together remain unresolved. The fiscal outlook adds urgency: European Commission projections show Latvia's deficit potentially reaching 4.3 percent of GDP by 2027, raising doubts about whether spending restraint alone can close the gap.
